topic: Server browser, game metadata and same-server detection (RoALT), checked 2026-10-24

findings.claim: GET games.roblox.com/v1/games/{placeId}/servers/{serverType} still works without a cookie, and Roblox's own current OpenAPI documents it with optional cookie auth.
findings.detail: Primary source: the OpenAPI embedded in https://create.roblox.com/docs/cloud/reference/domains/games (page last_updated 2026-10-23; the legacy URL /docs/cloud/legacy/games/v1 redirects there). operationId PublicServerBrowserService.GameInstances_GetServerList, security [{}, roblox-legacy-cookie]. Path params: placeId int64; serverType enum [0,1]. Live test: 0=Public, and the names 'Public' and 'Friend' are also accepted. Query params: sortOrder enum [1,2] (1=Asc, 2=Desc; 'Asc'/'Desc' strings also accepted), limit int32, cursor string, excludeFullGames bool (default false). Response GameServerResponsePageResponse: {previousPageCursor: string?, nextPageCursor: string?, data: [{id: uuid?, maxPlayers: int32, playing: int32, playerTokens: [string], players: [{id: int64, name?, displayName?, playerToken?}], fps: double?, ping: int32?, languageMatchCount: int32?, pingSignalLevel: 'Low'|'Medium'|'High', friendCount: int32?, name?, vipServerId: int64?, accessCode: uuid?, owner: {id, name, displayName, hasVerifiedBadge}}]}. Observed for unauthenticated v1 Public calls: only id, maxPlayers, playing, playerTokens ([]), players ([]), fps, ping. Documented errors: 400 and 404, with no further detail. The legacy JSON at prod.docsiteassets.roblox.com/assets/en-us/cloud/legacy/games/v1.json, and the old games.roblox.com/docs/json/v1 (now 404), do NOT include the servers routes. Only the create-docs embedded spec has them.

findings.claim: limit only accepts 10, 25, 50 or 100. The limit=100 empty-page bug from September 2025 is gone.
findings.detail: GET .../servers/Public?limit=20 returns HTTP 400 {"errors":[{"code":0,"message":"Allowed values: 10, 25, 50, 100","field":"limit"}]}. The OpenAPI only says int32. limit=100 returned 100 servers plus a nextPageCursor on 2026-10-24, both for v1 Asc on place 920587237 and for v2. DevForum topic 3930693 (2025-09-12) reported limit=100 returning data:[]. Staff (jpepsteve) replied the same day: 'This was not an intended change' and that it had recovered. A v2 call with no limit returned 10 items, so 10 looks like the default page size.

findings.claim: Without a cookie, each server-list route allows only 3 requests per 60 s per IP. The response headers expose this, and a 429 includes a misleading Retry-After.
findings.detail: All v1, v2 and alias server-list responses carry the headers 'x-ratelimit-limit: 3, 3;w=60', 'x-ratelimit-remaining: N' and 'x-ratelimit-reset: <seconds>'. The window is fixed: remaining refills to 2 after reset. 400 responses also use up quota. The 4th call in a window returns HTTP 429 with body {"errors":[{"code":0,"message":""}]} and the headers 'x-envoy-ratelimited: true', 'retry-after: 5' and 'x-retry-after-coverage: /v1/games/{placeId}/servers/{serverType}/', while x-ratelimit-reset was still 50. So the bucket is keyed on the route template, which means all placeIds share it, and Retry-After understates the wait. Separate buckets were observed for /v1/games/{placeId}/servers/*, /v2/games/{placeId}/servers/* and /v1/public-server-browser-service/games/{placeId}/servers/*: each showed remaining=2 while another was exhausted. Limits with a cookie were not tested. A January 2026 DevForum post says people send a cookie because of a 'hidden rate limit for unauthenticated requests'. A third-party blog (hproxy.com, about 2026-09) also reports 3/min/IP, which agrees with this but is unverified.

findings.claim: Logging in changes what the server list returns. Friend lists and the Recommended and BestLatency orders need a cookie, and guests get stripped fields. The announced logged-in-only rule is not enforced yet.
findings.detail: Observed without a cookie: GET /v2/games/920587237/servers/Friend and GET /v2/games/920587237/servers/Public?orderBy=BestLatency both return HTTP 400 {"errors":[{"code":7,"message":"Guest users are not allowed."}]}. Guest data has playerTokens:[] and players:[], v2 items carry friendCount:0 with no ping or pingSignalLevel, and v1 keeps ping. In the website bundle (ServerList.js on js.rbxcdn.com, fetched 2026-10-24), the sort dropdown only adds the 'Recommended' and 'BestLatency' options when isAuthenticated. Announcement '[Test] Updates to Server List Page' (DevForum topic 3966648, 2025-09-29, jpepsteve, Roblox User Team) plans to limit how many servers a user can browse and to limit the server list API to logged-in users only, affecting games.roblox.com/v1/games/{placeId}/servers/Public. As of 2026-10-24, guest v1 and v2 Public calls still return 200. Creators with edit access are exempt from the browse cap. Whether a cookie fills playerTokens or players was not checked. A 2024 report says at most 5 tokens per server.

findings.claim: The roblox.com website's server list now uses GET games.roblox.com/v2/games/{placeId}/servers/Public, sorted with orderBy rather than sortOrder.
findings.detail: In ServerList.js the public list calls `${gamesApi}/v2/games/${placeId}/servers/Public` with {cursor, ...options}, using withCredentials and retryable:true. Friends use v1 `/v1/games/${placeId}/servers/Friend`, or `/v2/games/${placeId}/servers/Friend` when the experiment flag isFriendsServerListV2Enabled is on. Private servers use `/v1/games/${placeId}/private-servers`. Sort map: {occupancyDesc:'OccupancyDesc', occupancyAsc:'OccupancyAsc', recommended:'Recommended', bestLatency:'BestLatency'}, default options {sortOrder:'Desc', excludeFullGames:false}. The OpenAPI (GameInstances_GetServerListV2) lists orderBy as enum ServerListSortOption [0,1,2,3,4] with no names, plus limit, cursor and excludeFullGames, and no sortOrder. Live: v2 ignores sortOrder (sortOrder=Asc still returned full 35/35 servers), and orderBy=OccupancyAsc&limit=100 returned 100 servers with playing=1. The website reads these per-item fields: id, maxPlayers, playing, players, playerTokens, pingSignalLevel, languageMatchCount, friendCount, name, vipServerId, accessCode, owner. At the top level it reads data, nextPageCursor and gameJoinRestricted. Cursor formats differ: v1 is base64 of '{"startIndex":10,"discriminator":"placeId:2753915549serverType:Public","count":10}\n<64-hex signature>' (offset based), while v2 is base64 protobuf holding the last server UUID (keyset based). Treat both as opaque. RoSeal (2026-08) and Froststrap (2026-10-21) also use v2. Froststrap sends sortOrder=Desc&excludeFullGames=true&limit=100&orderBy=BestLatency with a cookie.

findings.claim: A third route, /v1/public-server-browser-service/games/{placeId}/servers/{serverType}, behaves the same as v1 and has its own rate-limit bucket.
findings.detail: It is documented in the same OpenAPI (operationId GameInstances_GetServerList) with the same params as v1. Live without a cookie: 200 with fields fps, id, maxPlayers, ping, playerTokens, players, playing, and x-ratelimit-remaining 2 while the v1 bucket was partly used. There is no newer servers endpoint on apis.roblox.com. /servers/0 (numeric type) works on v1.

findings.claim: Paging repeats many servers, and the reported 700-server cap did not happen for an unauthenticated v1 Desc scan on 2026-10-24.
findings.detail: Walking v1 Public for place 2753915549 (sortOrder=Desc, limit=100), one request every 21 s: 11 pages returned 1100 rows but only 895 unique ids, with 12 to 37 repeats per page, and nextPageCursor was still set after page 11. The website's loader also merges pages by id. The DevForum report (2026-01-25) said nextPageCursor becomes null after about 700 servers. A reply on 2026-01-29 from Haydz6 (not shown as staff) called it 'intentional behaviour' and linked the server-list test. That report used a cookie. Whether the cap applies to authenticated requests, or only during the test, is unknown. MultiAlt independently saw '50 repeated in 400 servers'.

findings.claim: Open Cloud's game-server listing is for creators only and is not a usable server browser for arbitrary games.
findings.detail: The 'Revamped Server Restarts and Server Management' post (DevForum 4537709, 2026-03-25, Gryphscribe, Creator Services) links Open Cloud GameServers_ListGameServers. It filters on place_id, job_id, player_id, place_version, engine_version, memory_bytes_used, fps, occupancy, is_full, server_type, game_uptime and game_start_time. It needs Read permission on the experience, and the FAQ says the API has low rate limits and is for administration, not custom matchmaking. The exact OAuth or API-key scope name was not confirmed.

findings.claim: Place to universe: GET apis.roblox.com/universes/v1/places/{placeId}/universe returns {"universeId": <int|null>} without a cookie.
findings.detail: Live: placeId 2753915549 returns {"universeId":994732206}, while an invalid or nonexistent placeId returns HTTP 200 {"universeId":null}, not a 404. Headers: x-ratelimit-limit '60, 60;w=60'. The route is not in the create.roblox.com docs, but RoSeal (2026-08) uses it with cookies. A documented alternative is multiget-place-details (field universeId), which needs a cookie (see M4).

findings.claim: Game details: GET games.roblox.com/v1/games?universeIds=a,b (at most 50 ids, CSV) works without a cookie at 300 requests per minute. The live response differs from the spec in places.
findings.detail: Spec (legacy JSON plus create docs): universeIds is required, CSV, 'Cannot exceed a maximum of 50 IDs'. An optional 'fields' param is a comma-separated field list. Errors: 400 code 8 (invalid ids), 9 (too many), 429 code 4. Response {data:[GameDetailResponse]}. Live fields: id, rootPlaceId, name, description, sourceName, sourceDescription, creator{id,name,type,isRNVAccount,hasVerifiedBadge}, price (null when free), allowedGearGenres, allowedGearCategories, isGenreEnforced, copyingAllowed, playing, visits, maxPlayers, created, updated, studioAccessToApisAllowed, createVipServersAllowed, universeAvatarType, genre, genre_l1, genre_l2, untranslated_genre_l1, isAllGenre, isFavoritedByUser, favoritedCount, canonicalUrlPath, isContentRestricted, isOfficiallyLicensed, isCommunityLicensed. Differences: universeAvatarType comes back as a STRING ('MorphToR15') although the spec says integer, and isOfficiallyLicensed and isCommunityLicensed are not in the spec. Header 'x-ratelimit-limit: 300, 300;w=60'.

findings.claim: Game icons: thumbnails.roblox.com/v1/games/icons?universeIds= or /v1/places/gameicons?placeIds= work without a cookie and are marked STABLE. The place-based route skips the universe lookup.
findings.detail: Params: universeIds or placeIds (required, CSV); returnPolicy enum PlaceHolder|ForcePlaceHolder|AutoGenerated|ForceAutoGenerated (default PlaceHolder; the AutoGenerated policies return 403 code 9 without permission); size enum 50x50|128x128|150x150|256x256|420x420|512x512 (default 50x50); format Png|Jpeg|Webp|Ico|Icns (default Png); isCircular. Response {data:[{targetId, state:'Completed', imageUrl:'https://tr.rbxcdn.com/180DAY-<hash>/150/150/Image/Webp/noFilter', version:'TN3'}]}. Results are not in input order, so match on targetId. Invalid ids are 'filtered out', although universeId 1 still returned a placeholder GameIcon2 with state Completed. Rate headers: games/icons '1200, 1200;w=60', places/gameicons '60, 60;w=60'. Other 400 codes: 1 (too many ids), 2 (format), 3 (size), 4 (ids invalid), 8 (bad policy), 10 (circular not allowed).

findings.claim: GET games.roblox.com/v1/games/multiget-place-details?placeIds=1&placeIds=2 needs a .ROBLOSECURITY cookie.
findings.detail: Without a cookie: HTTP 401 {"errors":[{"code":9002,"subcode":0,"message":"Authentication token is missing"}]}, header x-ratelimit-limit '1000, 1000;w=60'. The array is repeated, not CSV (collectionFormat multi). Response [PlaceDetails{placeId, name, description, sourceName, sourceDescription, url, builder, builderId, hasVerifiedBadge, isPlayable, reasonProhibited, universeId, universeRootPlaceId, price, imageToken, fiatPurchaseData{localizedFiatPrice, basePriceId}}]. The spec tags it x-roblox-stability EXPERIMENTAL and gives no maximum count. RoSeal batches 50. isPlayable and reasonProhibited are per-account and useful for checking access before a launch.

findings.claim: GET games.roblox.com/v1/games/{placeId}/private-servers needs a cookie. It is marked EXPERIMENTAL, and each item carries accessCode only when the viewer can join.
findings.detail: Without a cookie: 401 code 9002, x-ratelimit-limit '9, 9;w=60'. OpenAPI (PrivateServers_GetPrivateServerList, EXPERIMENTAL): query params exclusiveStartKeyCursor (object {discriminator, count, key, sortOrder Asc|Desc, pagingDirection Forward|Backward, pageNumber}) and excludeFriendServers bool (default false). The website passes a plain 'cursor', and RoSeal passes limit, cursor and sortOrder, so the spec params look generated and inaccurate. Response GetPrivateServerListResponse {data:[{id:uuid? (jobId when running), maxPlayers, playing, playerTokens, players[{id,name,displayName,playerToken}], fps, ping, name, vipServerId:int64?, accessCode:uuid?, owner{id,name,displayName,hasVerifiedBadge}}], previousPageCursor, nextPageCursor, gameJoinRestricted:bool}. The website shows 'NoOneCanJoinServerDueToPrivacySettings' when vipServerId is set but accessCode is missing. Owners get subscription data from GET /v1/vip-servers/{id} (401 without a cookie; returns {id,name,game{id,name,rootPlace{id,name}},joinCode,active,subscription{...},permissions{clanAllowed,enemyClanId,friendsAllowed,users[]},link}). Also documented: GET /v1/private-servers/my-private-servers?privateServersTab=MyPrivateServers|OtherPrivateServers&itemsPerPage=25&cursor= and GET /v1/private-servers/enabled-in-universe/{universeId}, which works without a cookie and returns {privateServersEnabled}.

findings.claim: Presence only returns gameId to an authenticated viewer who is allowed to see or join the user. Whether a cookie querying its own userId gets its own gameId is not confirmed by any primary source.
findings.detail: POST https://presence.roblox.com/v1/presence/users with body {"userIds":[...]} works without a cookie and without CSRF: HTTP 200, 'x-ratelimit-limit: 60, 60;w=60'. OpenAPI (Presence_GetUserPresences, EXPERIMENTAL, security optional cookie): UserPresence {userPresenceType: 0|1|2|3 (0 offline, 1 website, 2 in game, 3 Studio), lastLocation, placeId?, rootPlaceId?, gameId: uuid?, universeId?, userId}. The old lastOnline field is gone. Without a cookie the game fields are null. MultiAlt (Tauri+Rust, 2026-10) documents: "the gameId ... only comes when the request carries an account's cookie". It also notes that what comes back depends on the viewer's friendship and the target's privacy. On 2025-04-25, staff (feriderk, Radicalius) rolled back a change that had exposed game data of users whose joins were set to Friends to non-friends, which confirms the intended rule is gated by the target's join privacy. For a self-query (cookie of account A asking for A), the result is probably full data, but this is inferred. Gotcha: gameId belongs to placeId (possibly a sub-place), not rootPlaceId. MultiAlt saw failed joins when it used rootPlaceId with a sub-place jobId.

findings.claim: Presence is slow and sometimes wrong. There is no documented update latency, and several reports describe in-game status missing for minutes.
findings.detail: DevForum 3678257 (2025): players show as online or offline while in game, sometimes for a minute and sometimes constantly. DevForum 3876124 (2025-08-12) has the staff reply feriderk 2025-08-13: 'We are rolling out improvements to the Presence system in the coming weeks.' No source gives a figure in seconds. MultiAlt's 'wait for player' feature polls presence every 30 s and honours Retry-After on 429. Treat presence as a slow secondary check, not the main way to detect the server.

findings.claim: The client log file is the earliest and most reliable local source of the jobId, and the log line formats are current as of client 0.743 (October 2026).
findings.detail:
Location: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Roblox\logs\*Player*.log, one file per RobloxPlayerBeta process, opened with FileShare.ReadWrite and tailed. Lines and regexes from Bloxstrap ActivityWatcher.cs (2026-08-05) and MultiAlt roblox_log.rs (calibrated on 0.743 logs, 2026-10-15): - `[FLog::Output] ! Joining game '' place at <10.x internal ip>`, regex `! Joining game '([0-9a-f\-]{36})' place ([0-9]+) at ([0-9\.]+)` - `[FLog::GameJoinLoadTime] Report game_join_loadtime: placeid:

, join_time:0.71, universeid:, referral_page:RequestGame, sid:, clienttime:, userid:,`, regex `universeid:([0-9]+).*userid:([0-9]+)`. Use this line to tie the log file to the account. - `[FLog::Network] UDMUX Address = , Port = | RCC Server Address = <10.x>, Port = ` - `[FLog::Network] Replicator created: ` / `serverId: |`, which marks the join as connected. - `[FLog::Network] Time to disconnect replication data:` and `[FLog::SingleSurfaceApp] leaveUGCGameInternal` mark leaving. - `[FLog::Output] Server Prefix: 0.743.0.7431129_20261014T203500Z_RCC_b25e4` gives the server start time. Bloxstrap picks the newest Player log created within 15 s of launch, which races when several clients start at once. Map by PID or by the userid line instead. Bloxstrap warns that the non-Output FLog lines are 'technically volatile' because they depend on FLog levels. 'Joining game' appears when the client gets its join response, before the world loads. The exact delay was not measured here. MultiAlt waits for 'in game' with an 8 s floor and a 20 s cap. Local logs were not inspected, because the task did not allow it.

findings.claim: For bulk launch, a maintained Tauri peer (MultiAlt) avoids detection entirely by choosing one jobId before launching anyone. Following account #1 is a second option.
findings.detail: MultiAlt server-choice.md (2026-10): it picks one server for the whole batch from the public list (excludeFullGames=true, sort by preference, scanning up to 6 Desc pages for 'best fit') so that playing + batchSize <= maxPlayers, preferring one spare slot. Every account then joins the same jobId with PlaceLauncher request=RequestGameJob&gameId=<jobId>. It keeps an 8 s minimum gap between accounts ('anti-captcha'). The alternative is PlaceLauncher request=RequestFollowUser&userId=<account1Id>, with the website's followPlayerIntoGame or gamejoin /v1/play-with-user {userIdToFollow}. Roblox then resolves the server, but account #1's 'who can join me' setting must allow the followers. MultiAlt uses this by default and claims it 'helps avoid CAPTCHA'; that claim comes from the owner and is unverified. ic3w0lf22/Roblox-Account-Manager was archived 2024-10-01 and is stale.

findings.claim: The gamejoin endpoints are undocumented, v1 only (/v2 returns 404 today), and need a cookie, except join-game, which returns 200 with status 12 when no cookie is sent.
findings.detail: gamejoin is not on create.roblox.com: /docs/cloud/legacy/gamejoin/v1 returns 404 and the docsiteassets JSON returns 403. Without a cookie, POST https://gamejoin.roblox.com/v1/join-game-instance, /v1/join-private-game and /v1/play-with-user return 401 {code:9002,'Authentication token is missing'}. /v1/join-game returns 200 {jobId:null,status:12,statusData:null,joinScriptUrl:null,authenticationUrl:null,authenticationTicket:null,message:'Unable to join Game 212',joinScript:null,joinTicket:null,queuePosition:0}. /v2/join-game-instance and /v2/join-game return 404 now. RoValra's commits show a gamejoin v2 was live around 2026-07-01 and was removed from use on 2026-09-20. RoValra still parses text/event-stream responses (event 'ResponseReady'). Rate header 'x-ratelimit-limit: 5, 5;w=1', i.e. 5 per second. Request bodies, from RoZod (generated from Roblox swagger, undated) and RoSeal: join-game-instance {placeId, gameId, gameJoinAttemptId, isTeleport, joinOrigin, browserTrackerId, isPlayTogetherGame, isQueueAllowedOverride, channelName, partyId, gamerTag, isImmersiveAdsTeleport, cId}; join-game {placeId, gameIdToExclude, eventId, isoContext, ...common}; join-private-game {placeId, accessCode, linkCode, ...}; join-reserved-game {placeId, accessCode, cId, ...}; play-with-user {userIdToFollow, ...}. The response includes joinTicket, which RoZod lacks, so RoZod is partly stale. statusData can be {creatorExperienceBan{startTime,durationSeconds,displayReason,displayReasonTextFilterStatus,isInherited}}. joinScript has PascalCase keys including GameId, PlaceId, UniverseId, DataCenterId, MachineAddress, UdmuxEndpoints[{Address,Port}], ServerConnections, ClientTicket, SessionId and ServerClaimedTime.

findings.claim: Join status codes come from community sources, not Roblox: 2 means a server was found and the join data loaded; 6 means server full; 12 means not allowed; 22 means queued, which tools treat as 'full'.
findings.detail: RoSeal JoinServerStatusCode (2026-08-26): 0 Retry, 1 ServerFound, 2 ServerDataLoaded, 3 ExperienceDisabled, 4 ServerUnavailable, 5 ServerUnavailableUnexpectedly, 6 ServerFull, 10 FollowedUserLeft, 11 ExperienceRestricted, 12 NoPermission, 13 ServerBusy, 14 HashExpired, 15 HashException, 16 PartyTooLarge, 17 HTTPError, 18 MalformedRequestBody, 19 ChannelMismatch, 20 SetChannelInternalOnly, 21 UnauthorizedPrivacySettings, 22 InQueue, 23 UserBanned. Message mapping: 'Unable to join Game 211..811' = RequestDenied, '...212..812' = NotAuthenticated, 'Game instance cannot be joined' / 'Could not find requested game instance' = InvalidServer, 'User privacy does not allow join.', 'You need to purchase access to this game before you can play.', and others. Tools disagree on 'full': BTRoblox (2026-04) treats status 22 as 'Server is full' and 12 as 'no access to this place'; RoValra (2026-09) counts 2 or 22 as 'server active'; Froststrap (2026-10-21) counts only status==2 as alive; MultiAlt treats 12 as denied (error 524) and 6 as full. Do not rely on the message text, which is localized; branch on status.

findings.claim: gamejoin checks the User-Agent. A 'Roblox/...' UA is the norm, and CSRF does not seem to be required.
findings.detail: Observed without a cookie on POST /v1/join-game: UA 'Roblox/WinInet' or 'Roblox/RoALT' gives message 'Unable to join Game 212' (NotAuthenticated). A browser UA or the curl default gives 'Unable to join Game 211' (RequestDenied). So a non-Roblox UA is turned away on a different code path. BTRoblox explicitly rewrites the UA to 'Roblox/WinInet' for join-game-instance through declarativeNetRequest, Froststrap sets 'Roblox/Froststrap', and a 2024 DevForum script used 'Roblox/WinInet'. CSRF: BTRoblox (fetch with credentials:'include') and Froststrap (Cookie, Referer https://roblox.com/games/{placeId}, Origin https://roblox.com) send no X-CSRF-TOKEN. RoValra sends one for every POST. Requests without a cookie never got a CSRF 403, but that does not prove an authenticated request skips it. Handle a 403 with an x-csrf-token header by retrying with it.

findings.claim: join-game-instance works as a per-account 'can this account join this server' check before launching, but it is a real join request: it returns live join credentials, and bursts get rate limited.
findings.detail: With status 2 the response contains a full joinScript, including ClientTicket and SessionId, which must be treated as secrets and thrown away. It does not start a client. Whether it briefly reserves a slot is unknown. RoValra reads joinScript.ServerClaimedTime for server uptime. MultiAlt warns that resolving regions in bursts 'gets 429 and flags the account', so it spaces calls about 0.9 s apart with at most 40 per request and checks access once per account per place, because access is usually a place rule, not a server rule. RoValra spaces gamejoin calls at least 100 ms apart, times out at 2 s, and treats a timeout as status 22. Froststrap retries 429/5xx up to 3 times (500 ms x attempt). Region: use joinScript.UdmuxEndpoints[0].Address (public 128.116.x.x) and fall back to MachineAddress only if it is public, since MachineAddress is usually an internal 10.x address. DataCenterId maps to a region through a datacenter table that the community maintains.

open_questions: With a .ROBLOSECURITY cookie, what do the v1 and v2 server lists return? Are playerTokens and players filled (at most 5?), is ping present in v2, what are the rate-limit headers (still 3/60 s, or per user?), and does the roughly 700-server pagination cap from January 2026 apply to authenticated calls?

Does POST presence/v1/presence/users with account A's cookie, asking about A itself, return A's gameId? Does that change when A's 'who can join me' is set to No one? What is the typical delay between the 'Joining game' log line and presence showing gameId?

Names for ServerListSortOption values 0 to 4 on v2 orderBy. The strings OccupancyDesc, OccupancyAsc, Recommended and BestLatency are confirmed to work. What is the fifth value (default or unspecified?) and the default order?
Does an authenticated gamejoin POST ever require X-CSRF-TOKEN? Does a non-'Roblox/' UA with a valid cookie get status 12 / 'Unable to join Game 211'?
For a full public server, does join-game-instance return 6 (ServerFull) or 22 (InQueue)? Does isQueueAllowedOverride change that? Does a status-2 pre-check hold or reserve a slot?
Will the gamejoin v2 / text/event-stream response format (briefly live around mid-2026 per RoValra) come back, and when is SSE returned on v1?
Is the 'Recommended'/'BestLatency' ordering or the server-list browse cap tied to an experiment (ixp) that can differ per account?
What exact OAuth/API-key scope and rate limit does Open Cloud GameServers_ListGameServers use? (Relevant only if RoALT ever lists servers for the user's own experiences.)
design_implications: Server browser: call GET games.roblox.com/v2/games/{placeId}/servers/Public?orderBy=OccupancyDesc|OccupancyAsc&excludeFullGames=true&limit=100, with the selected account's cookie when one is available (needed for BestLatency, Recommended and Friend). Keep v1 /servers/{Public|Friend}?sortOrder=Asc|Desc&limit=… as a fallback. Accept only limit 10, 25, 50 or 100.

Rate limiting: run a per-route token bucket driven by x-ratelimit-remaining and x-ratelimit-reset. On 429, wait for x-ratelimit-reset, not 'retry-after: 5'. Plan for 3 requests per minute per route per IP without a cookie, which makes a 30-page scan take about 10 minutes. Scan pages lazily and on demand, not as a full crawl.
Treat cursors as opaque strings. Deduplicate servers by id across pages (12 to 37 repeats per 100-server page were observed). Stop on a null nextPageCursor and also at a user-set page cap.

Deserialize leniently. Every server field except id, maxPlayers and playing can be missing or null. universeAvatarType comes back as a string even though the spec says int. Unknown fields such as isOfficiallyLicensed must not break parsing. Tolerate Roblox adding pingSignalLevel, languageMatchCount and friendCount.

Metadata pipeline: placeId → apis.roblox.com/universes/v1/places/{placeId}/universe (no cookie, 60/min, null means invalid) → games.roblox.com/v1/games?universeIds=<≤50 CSV> (300/min) plus thumbnails /v1/places/gameicons?placeIds=…&size=150x150&format=Png, which needs no universe. Cache aggressively, and match icons by targetId. Use multiget-place-details with a cookie only when per-account isPlayable or reasonProhibited is needed.

Private servers: call GET /v1/games/{placeId}/private-servers?cursor=… with a cookie. Show a server as joinable only when accessCode is present. Respect gameJoinRestricted. Launch with PlaceLauncher request=RequestPrivateGame&placeId=…&accessCode=…&linkCode=….

Bulk launch into the same server: pick the jobId BEFORE launching. Choose a server where playing + N <= maxPlayers, ideally with one spare slot, then launch every account with RequestGameJob&gameId=<jobId>. This removes the detection problem, and it is what the maintained Tauri peer MultiAlt does.

When Roblox matchmaking chose account #1's server: read the jobId by tailing that client's log for "[FLog::Output] ! Joining game '<uuid>' place <id>". Bind the log file to the account through PID or the GameJoinLoadTime 'userid:' line, not by 'newest file'. Use authenticated presence with account #1's own cookie only as a slower cross-check (self-query not verified). Use place-level placeId from presence, not rootPlaceId.

Following account #1 (RequestFollowUser&userId=<account1>) is a cheap alternative for accounts 2..N, but only works when account #1's join privacy allows them. Expose it as an option, not the default, until it is verified.

A gamejoin pre-check (POST gamejoin.roblox.com/v1/join-game-instance {placeId, gameId, gameJoinAttemptId:uuid}, UA 'Roblox/WinInet', cookie, no CSRF unless challenged) is useful for 'can this account join' and for region (UdmuxEndpoints[0].Address). Run it once per account per place, at least 1 s apart, branch on numeric status (2 ok, 6 or 22 full or queued, 12 no permission), and never log or store the returned joinScript or ClientTicket.

Keep all Roblox endpoint URLs and status mappings in one data table, not scattered through code. The servers v1→v2 move, gamejoin v2 appearing and then being removed, and the announced logged-in-only server list all changed within the last 13 months.
Leave out region filtering by default. Each server's region costs one gamejoin call plus an IP-to-geo lookup with a third-party service, and RoALT is local-only.
